Question.title: Question
Question.description: Represents a question submitted by an attendee for a specific session.

sessionId.description: Reference to Session. (Relationship: Session 1:N Question) The ID of the session this question belongs to.

attendeeId.description: Reference to Attendee. (Relationship: Attendee 1:N Question) The ID of the attendee who submitted the question.

text.description: The text content of the question.

timestamp.description: The date and time the question was submitted.

isAnswered.description: Indicates whether the question has been answered.

Poll.title: Poll
Poll.description: Represents a live poll created for a specific session.

sessionId.description: Reference to Session. (Relationship: Session 1:N Poll) The ID of the session this poll belongs to.

questionText.description: The text of the poll question.

options.description: An array of possible answer options for the poll.

startTime.description: The date and time the poll started.

endTime.description: The date and time the poll ended.

PollResponse.title: PollResponse
PollResponse.description: Represents a single response to a poll from an attendee.

id.description: Unique identifier for the poll response.

pollId.description: Reference to Poll. (Relationship: Poll 1:N PollResponse) The ID of the poll this response belongs to.

attendeeId.description: Reference to Attendee. (Relationship: Attendee 1:N PollResponse) The ID of the attendee who submitted the response.

selectedOption.description: The text of the option selected by the attendee.

timestamp.description: The date and time the response was submitted.

Session.title: Session
Session.description: Represents a session in the leadership summit agenda.

time.description: The time slot of the session (e.g., '9:00 AM - 10:00 AM').

speaker.description: The name of the speaker for the session.

content.description: The duration of the content portion of the session in minutes.

qa.description: The duration of the Q&A portion of the session in minutes.

prayer.description: The duration of the prayer portion of the session in minutes.

afternoon.description: Indicates whether the session takes place in the afternoon.

summary.description: A brief summary of the session content.

Attendee.title: Attendee
Attendee.description: Represents an attendee of the leadership summit.

firstName.description: The first name of the attendee.

lastName.description: The last name of the attendee.

email.description: The email address of the attendee.

affiliation.description: The organization or group the attendee is affiliated with.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to support real-time Q&A and polling features for the leadership summit, emphasizing security, scalability, and ease of debugging. It leverages denormalization to ensure authorization independence and structural segregation to maintain a homogeneous security posture across collections.

**Authorization Independence:**  Each document that requires authorization context (e.g., Questions, PollResponses) includes the `sessionId` and/or `attendeeId`. This denormalization avoids the need for `get()` calls in security rules, allowing atomic operations (transactions/batches) and simplifying debugging.

**QAPs Support:**
*   **Questions:** Stored in a subcollection under `sessions/{sessionId}/questions/{questionId}`. This allows listing questions specific to a session, and rules can easily ensure that only authenticated users can create questions within a session.
*   **Polls:** Stored in a subcollection under `sessions/{sessionId}/polls/{pollId}`.  This allows for listing polls specific to a session.
*   **PollResponses:**  Stored in a subcollection under `polls/{pollId}/responses/{responseId}`. This allows for listing poll responses specific to a poll and user. The security rules can enforce that each attendee can only submit one response per poll by checking `request.auth.uid` against `attendeeId`.

**Structural Segregation:** The data is segregated into collections and subcollections based on entity relationships. This ensures that all documents within a collection share the same security requirements. For example, all questions in `sessions/{sessionId}/questions` are associated with a specific session and accessible to attendees. All polls are managed at `sessions/{sessionId}/polls/{pollId}`.  All poll responses are managed at `polls/{pollId}/responses/{responseId}`.

**Access Modeling:**
*   **Path-Based Ownership:**  Attendee-generated content (Questions, PollResponses) are implicitly owned via the `attendeeId` field.

**Invariants:**  The structure supports the integrity of ownership (via `attendeeId` and `sessionId`), timestamps (via `timestamp` fields), and denormalized data. Security rules can enforce that these fields are immutable after creation.
